title: The Opposition Could Not Beat Morena in 2027
author: Pedro Mellado Rodríguez
content:
_This article by[Pedro Mellado
Rodríguez](https://www.sinembargo.mx/author/pedromellado/) originally appeared
in the [September 11, 2026 edition of
SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4868199/oposicion-no-podria-vencer-a-
morena-en-2027/), an independent Mexican digital news outlet._

The opposition parties that will appear on the ballots in the elections of
Sunday, June 6, 2027, must abandon all hope of defeating Morena to strip it of
its majority in the Chamber of Deputies. That is what the most recent polls
say, anticipating that the PAN and PRI, together, would not reach enough
votes. And slipping in between them would be Movimiento Ciudadano, which would
very likely displace the National Action Party (PAN) from second place as a
political force in the country.

Polling exercises carried out by the firms Enkoll and Buendía & Márquez
conclude that Morena’s voting margin in their September 2026 measurements
ranges between **35 and 41 percent**. Meanwhile the PAN reaches its best
showing with 12 percent, the same as Movimiento Ciudadano, while the PRI’s
best performance tops out at nine percent. Morena’s presumed ally, the
Ecologist Green Party of Mexico (PVEM), registers between three and five
percent support.

The average turnout in the six midterm elections to choose federal deputies in
our country between 1991 and 2021 is 51.69 percent. If we round it to 52
percent, we could estimate that, out of an Electoral Roll of just over 100
million citizens, a little more than 52 million people could go to the polls
on Sunday, June 6, 2027. The Electoral Roll as of this past Thursday, August
28, 2026, had 100,862,772 citizens registered with a valid voter ID.

This past Wednesday, September 2, 2026, the consulting firm Enkoll published a
poll concluding that 41 percent of citizens would vote for the Morena party in
the contest for the federal Chamber of Deputies. Out of an estimated turnout
of 52 million people, that percentage favoring Morena would represent 21
million votes.

The National Action Party would capture 12 percent; Movimiento Ciudadano would
add the same percentage, and the PRI would have eight percent of popular
support. In total, the opposition as a whole would have 32 percent. But if
Movimiento Ciudadano went its own way, to try to take second place as a
political force in the country from the PAN, the PAN-PRI opposition would be
left with only 20 percent.

In this way, the PAN and PRI would add up to just over 10 million votes, and
on its own Movimiento Ciudadano would have a little more than six million
votes. With three percent, the Green Party would reach a million and a half
votes, and with two percent the Labor Party (PT) would barely add up to one
million votes.

The PT and PVEM would be at risk of losing their registration if they ran
separately from the coalition that Morena led in the previous electoral
process. And they could even lose the votes that citizens have handed them as
a generous tribute for their presumed support of the Fourth Transformation
project, since many Morena supporters already see them as traitors to the
cause.

On the other hand, in the scenario laid out by the poll conducted by the firm
Buendía & Márquez, published this past Monday, September 7, 2026, Morena would
capture 35 percent of the votes in next year’s elections, something like 18
million votes, while, together, the PAN with 11 percent and the PRI with nine
percent would add up to 20 percent of the potential votes, for just over 10
million ballots.

Movimiento Ciudadano, with nine percent, according to Buendía & Márquez, would
add up to a little more than four and a half million votes. The Green Party
could achieve five percent of the votes, around two and a half million
ballots, while with two percent of the votes, the Labor Party would lose its
registration.

But there are other factors that must be taken into account. Morena currently
governs **23 states of the Republic** , in which 214 relative-majority seats
will be contested and where the maroon party will have every advantage. In 17
of those 23 states, Morena won in 2024 all the relative-majority seats that
were at stake, totaling 108 seats.

In another six states that Morena currently governs, the maroon party lost
only one of all the relative-majority seats contested in each of those states.
The PAN, PRI, and PRD won only one relative-majority seat each in Durango, the
State of Mexico, Michoacán, Tamaulipas, Veracruz, and Yucatán.

The opposition would only have a chance to defeat Morena and win relative-
majority and proportional-representation seats in the First Electoral
Constituency, where the maroon party governs only five of eight states. In
this region the PAN governs Chihuahua; the PRI runs Durango, and Movimiento
Ciudadano, Jalisco.

But the opposition’s greatest strength for winning relative-majority and
proportional-representation seats is in the Second Constituency, where the
opposition governs four of seven states: the PAN rules in Aguascalientes and
Guanajuato; the PRI runs Coahuila, and Movimiento Ciudadano holds the
executive branch in Nuevo León.

The majority of the proportional-representation seats in the three remaining
Electoral Constituencies will go to Morena, which runs the seven state
governments that make up the Third Constituency; in the Fourth Constituency
the six states that comprise it are also governed by the maroon party, and in
the Fifth Constituency, three of the four states have Morena governments,
including the State of Mexico, the state with the most votes and the most
electoral districts, with 40. In this Fifth Constituency the PAN governs
Querétaro, one of the four states that make it up, where Morena and its allies
won three of six relative-majority districts in the 2024 federal deputy
elections.

If you observe what is published on social media, and in particular what daily
saturates X, formerly Twitter, you might conclude that the world and the
country are falling apart, and that the activism of certain PAN, PRI, or
Movimiento Ciudadano figures will steer their parties toward a stunning
victory in 2027. However, in the real world, the presence of most of those
parties and those politicians is very far from the activism they display in
cyberspace.

In 2027, Morena’s party structure will be a crushing machine. This past
Monday, August 31, 2026, the Prerogatives and Political Parties Commission of
the National Electoral Institute (INE) presented its report on the triennial
validation of the membership rolls of the national political parties.
Councilor Carla Astrid Humphrey Jordan noted that having affiliated members is
fundamental because they constitute the basis of a party’s legitimacy of
origin, its operating structure, and its foundation in the country’s
democratic system.

And on that terrain, it is the Morena party that shows enormous strength,
officially registering **11,629,541 members** , who will be the basis of a
crushing electoral structure in the elections of Sunday, June 6, 2027, when
the country will vote for 500 new federal deputies, 17 governors, as well as
local deputies in 31 states and municipal presidents in 30 states.

Far behind is the opposition party that comes closest to Morena, in this case
the PRI, with 819,103 affiliated citizens. In total, Morena holds **75.44
percent** of the members that the eight officially registered parties add up
to across the Republic.

Even in the four states currently run by the opposition and where the
governorships will be renewed, Morena also has a wide advantage in terms of
its party structure. It surpasses the PAN in Aguascalientes, Chihuahua, and
Querétaro, and has a comfortable lead over Movimiento Ciudadano in Nuevo León.

As can be seen, there is no reference point that would suggest the opposition
is in a favorable position to pull off a surprise in the 2027 elections, much
less that it could strip Morena of its majority. The poverty reflected in the
polls prefigures a very adverse scenario, particularly for the PAN and PRI.
Even without its highly questionable partners, the PT and PVEM, Morena could
win the majority in the next Chamber of Deputies of the Congress of the Union.
